properties.statement: THE PROPOSED MERGE WOULD HAVE DELETED A `critical`/`proposed` REQUIREMENT IN FAVOUR OF AN UNRELATED `accepted` ONE, BECAUSE SURVIVOR SELECTION CONSULTS NEITHER PRIORITY NOR STATUS. Reported 2026-08-08 by w-9d1d1499 (dev_storyflow, LANE PROSE-JOIN) — a fourth independent seat reaching the duplicate-detector conclusion. They read BOTH nodes of one pair rather than trusting the score. `req:graph_is_the_content_bible`, priority CRITICAL, status PROPOSED: characters, locations, events, dimensions, dialogue, props and factions flow FROM the graph INTO every rendered panel, so rendered media is grounded rather than re-invented per render. `req:backend_as_product`, priority medium, status ACCEPTED: any authorized client - third-party frontend, phone app, CLI, editor plugin - can consume the narrative-graph capabilities WITHOUT our UI, API key with per-key rate tiers and a daily ingest budget. One is about grounding rendered media; the other about strangers building against a public API. NO SHARED REQUIREMENT, SURFACE OR ACTOR — the similarity is prose alone. TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS IN ONE CASE. (1) SCORING: name/prose similarity with no weighting by shared referents (actors, surfaces, components), so two requirements that touch nothing in common score as covering the same ground. (2) DIRECTION: the destructive half lands on the more load-bearing node. dec:merge-survivor-provenance settles the survivor by PROVENANCE with id breaking ties, and neither priority nor status is consulted anywhere in that rule — so an accepted, medium-priority node can eat a critical one that is still awaiting the user's word, which is exactly the certainty dec:certainty-derived says a status carries. THIS IS THE HALF PR #99 DID NOT COVER, and the distinction matters: #99 made a heuristic edge non-mergeable, so this case no longer proceeds automatically — but the moment a human DOES assert a duplicate, the same rule still picks the same survivor. FIX SHAPE, theirs: weight similarity by shared referents rather than prose; and never propose a merge that deletes a higher-priority or differently-statused node without saying so in the proposal.
